title: Database backup and restore command walkthrough
notes: Session dominated by shell commands for a multi-step DB backup/restore procedure, mirroring fx12's structure and spirit with a different scenario.

turns.text: Walk me through the backup and restore process for the Postgres prod DB, I always forget the exact flags.

Sure. To take a compressed backup: pg_dump -Fc -h prod-db.internal -U backup_user memories_db -f backup_2026_07_09.dump. The -Fc custom format is required for parallel restore later, plain SQL dumps can't do that.
Where should that file end up?

Upload it to the backup bucket right after: aws s3 cp backup_2026_07_09.dump s3://prod-db-backups/daily/backup_2026_07_09.dump — the daily/ prefix is what the lifecycle policy uses to expire backups after 30 days automatically.
And restoring, if we ever need to?

First pull it back down: aws s3 cp s3://prod-db-backups/daily/backup_2026_07_09.dump ./restore.dump — then restore into a NEW database, never directly over prod: pg_restore -h prod-db.internal -U backup_user -d memories_db_restore_test -j 4 restore.dump. The -j 4 flag parallelizes the restore across 4 jobs, which only works because we used -Fc on the way out.
How do we verify the restore actually worked before trusting it?

Run a row-count sanity check against a few key tables: psql -h prod-db.internal -U backup_user -d memories_db_restore_test -c "SELECT count(*) FROM memories;" and compare it against the same query run on prod at backup time — they should match closely, allowing for writes that happened between backup and restore.
Good, write that whole flow down.

Documented: dump with -Fc, upload to S3 under the daily/ prefix, restore into a separate test database (never overwrite prod directly) with pg_restore -j 4, then verify with a row-count sanity check against prod.

gold_atoms.text: The daily/ S3 prefix is what the bucket's lifecycle policy uses to automatically expire backups after 30 days.
The -j 4 parallel restore flag for pg_restore only works because the backup was taken with pg_dump's -Fc custom format — a plain SQL dump can't be restored in parallel.
Always restore backups into a new, separate database (e.g. memories_db_restore_test), never directly over the production database.
psql -h prod-db.internal -U backup_user -d memories_db_restore_test -c "SELECT count(*) FROM memories;"
